activities.name: Sunrise light on bare eyes and skin
activities.summary: Be outside every morning as the sun rises, with its first light on bare eyes and skin — he treats the eye as a timing organ, not only a camera.
steps: Get up before sunrise so you are outside when the sun clears the horizon.
Take off sunglasses, contact lenses and glasses, and don't watch from behind window glass — bare eyes need the morning ultraviolet-A and near-infrared for the retinal clock pathway.
Face east toward the rising sun, without staring straight into it.
Uncover as much skin as you reasonably can.

Stand barefoot at the same time — surf, wet sand, dewy grass or basalt (see “Barefoot grounding, done right”), ideally where the local field lies flatter against the ground. Variations: face east on all fours while grounded ("mammalian sphinxing"), or lie with your spine on the ground.
Stay 30–45 minutes, within the first 60–90 minutes after sunrise; longer is fine, up to about three hours on a beach.
Repeat every morning.
Watch for a well-formed (Bristol type 4) stool as a sign the routine is working.
For brain fog, pair this routine with dropping chemical fixes and switching routers off before sleep.
activities.cautions: Indoor "sun lamps" and watching sunrise through glass do not replace bare-eye, barefoot outdoor morning light in his model.

activities.name: Midday sun and UV-B, unfiltered
activities.summary: Get regular midday sun, UV-B included, on bare skin with no sunscreen or sunglasses, stopping before any redness.
steps: Go out near solar noon, when your shadow is shorter than you are.
Expose torso and back (for women, the breasts too); tan with bare skin, not through clothing, and go nude where you can.
Leave off sunscreen, sunglasses, contacts and glasses outdoors — he treats chemical sunscreen as a photon shield that blinds the eye's oxygen/field sensing (neuropsin), not only a UV cream.
Stand barefoot on the ground while you do it.
Build your time up gradually; move into shade or put on light clothing at the first warmth.
Prioritize midday UV-B around the winter solstice, and if you are not yet "pinned" (grounded, sunlit and living under a stable local magnetic field).
For dry skin, use morning sun, cold exposure and grounding rather than lotion or extra drinking water.
After a shower, use at most tallow or coconut oil — no petroleum- or silicone-based lotions, and no moisturizers with hidden UV filters.
Go out on cloudy days too.
Northern maternal lineages (such as haplogroup H) living in the tropics: avoid long exposure between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. unless you are moving or grounded.
A sunny latitude only helps if you are actually outdoors in it; staying pale means you aren't getting enough.

Treat midday UV-B as the Vitamin D receptor's environmental switch: real photons on bare skin while grounded, not an oral D3 pill as a stand-in — he also ties that UV-B/VDR step to pulling Complexes I and III out of a Marcus jam and to better night sleep after a full-spectrum day. He says sunlight never overdoses vitamin D because the local magnetic field steers the radical-pair cutoff; pills do not share that cutoff.
activities.cautions: Never burn on purpose; if you redden, cut back. Don't use sunscreen or sunglasses. Leave UV-C lamps alone. Oral vitamin D does not replace UV-driven receptor geometry in his model.

activities.name: Four-phase sun day (building a "solar callus")
activities.summary: A timed daily light schedule — sunrise, mid-morning, midday and sunset — for adapting skin to strong or tropical sun without burning.
steps: Sunrise phase: within 60–90 minutes after the sun clears the horizon, spend 30–45 minutes in its deep red and near-infrared light (no UV yet) with bare eyes and as much bare skin as possible, feet on volcanic basalt or wet black sand.
Mid-morning UV-A phase (about 8:30–11:00, depending on season and place): 15–25 minutes with skin and eyes open to the sky while walking or moving; never sunglasses, contacts or glasses.
Midday UV-B phase (shadow shorter than your height, about 11:30–1:30): 3–10 minutes at most on torso and back while grounded on bare rock.
If you're not yet adapted, start the midday phase at 3 minutes and add 1 minute every few days as your tan deepens.
At the first slight sting or warmth, move into shade or put on long, light clothing.
Sunset phase: in the last hour of daylight, 20–30 minutes of skin exposure to red and infrared (no UV) while winding down.
Even once adapted, avoid artificial light at night and out-of-season food eaten under the noon sun.
Optional: saffron, to speed adaptation.
activities.equipmentDetail: none (basalt or black sand ideal)
activities.cautions: Never let skin redden. Northern / uncoupled lineages (such as H, J, T, U) moving into tropical sun should acclimate gradually — in his model they run a high internal light output with little melanin shielding, so skip long ungrounded midday sessions until the solar callus builds. Keep sunrise and mid-morning phases; don't jump straight to hard noon UV.

activities.name: Sunset light
activities.summary: Spend 20–30 minutes outside in the last hour of daylight, with bare skin and no sunglasses.
steps: In the final hour of daylight, go outdoors for 20–30 minutes.
Keep skin bare and wear no sunglasses.
Watch the light fade from amber toward blue; an orange LED is no substitute.
Use it to wind down; after dark, follow “Evening light: incandescent, red, dark”.

activities.name: Evening light: incandescent, red, dark
activities.summary: After sunset, use only warm, blue-free light; in daylight, never block blue.
steps: Replace LED and fluorescent bulbs with incandescent ones.
In daylight, wear no blue blockers of any tint, red or yellow included.
By day, open a window rather than buying lamps that imitate the sun.
After sunset, switch to red incandescent bulbs or wear glasses that block 100% of blue and green light.
Don't eat sugary food under screens or LEDs at night.
Never wear sunglasses. If you wear contact lenses, go back to glasses, and take the glasses off whenever you're outdoors.

Sleep in total darkness, with no artificial light at night — he treats night blue on the retina as a false "day" signal that crashes melatonin and over-wakes alerting pathways, desynchronizing body clocks.
Don't switch on artificial light before sunrise; let daylight come first, every day.
activities.equipmentDetail: incandescent and red bulbs; 100% blue-blocking glasses
activities.cautions: Phone and screen light on the eyes after dark undoes morning eye timing; keep devices out of the bedroom (see “Cut screen time”).

activities.name: Cut screen time
activities.summary: Spend less time under blue-lit screens, above all before exercise and at night.
steps: Cut indoor screen and wireless time, including feeds.
When you do go online, use a wired connection and a low-blue "daylight" screen.
Don't go straight from TV or screens into a workout.
Keep devices out of the bedroom.
Indoors at screens and under artificial light only (never outdoors), wear lenses that filter 400–465 nm; yellow syntonic lenses work as a stopgap.
Keep phone light away from your eyes, above all at night.
activities.equipmentDetail: none (optional low-blue screen; 400–465 nm filtering lenses for indoor screen work)

activities.name: Sun first, red-light panels second
activities.summary: Get red and near-infrared light from the sun first, and use a panel only where sun is lacking.
steps: Get red and infrared from sunrise and daylight first; with hours of daily sun, a panel is unnecessary.
In the tropics, skip light devices and use the sun.
Firelight is another natural infrared-rich source.
Don't rely on single-wavelength devices.

If you use a panel: 660 and 850 nm, 30 minutes a day before exercise (see “Pin first, then light, then exercise and diet”). Use red light in the morning; afternoon sessions do little. If the device can pulse, set it to 40 Hz.

At high latitude (around 48°N and above): red/NIR daily, above all in winter, then maximize morning UV-A and midday UV-B through the summer — he treats morning red/IR as rehydrating melanin that blue light and weak winter sun dry out.
If you're deuterium-loaded, rebuild with red and near-infrared before leaning on UV.
Targeted uses: 670 nm on the chest and sternum for a strained voice; 670 nm rather than blue light when trying to bring blood sugar down.
Where sun is scarce, a daily infrared sauna dome can fill in; watch children closely for overheating, and prefer tropical sun where possible.
activities.equipmentDetail: optional 660/850 nm panel
activities.cautions: Fix grounding and your local field first; infrared can't make up for them. He treats NIR as a low-friction lubricant for the mitochondrial proton wave, not the sole driver of the ATP motor — still need sun geometry, UV-B by day, and a cold dark night. Don't combine methylene blue with 670/830 nm light unless you are grounded and away from wireless and blue light.

activities.name: Drinking water: reverse osmosis plus UV
activities.summary: Drink reverse-osmosis water with a UV stage, or clean deep-source water; avoid hard, mineral-heavy, fluoridated or surface water.
steps: Filter drinking water by reverse osmosis followed by a UV stage.
Avoid fluoride.
Avoid municipal water lines in heavily wired urban areas, and surface-runoff river water.
Don't rehydrate on hard, metal-laden well water.

Prefer deep "primary water" (from fissures in volcanic rock) or ancient artesian wells to surface water; clean local spring water drunk in the sun is a good natural mineral source. Judge a bottled spring water (such as Mountain Valley) by the hydrology of its source; desert sources count against it.
Never drink from the Riviera Maya cenote system. On Central America's Pacific side, make a new water plan, since local rain is getting heavier in deuterium.
Prefer copper plumbing to plastic.
Store drinking water in large copper vessels and let it sit 4–16 hours before drinking.
If local animals show signs of decline, switch to deep aquifer water (see “Track your local field”).
activities.equipmentDetail: RO filter with UV stage; optional copper storage vessels

activities.name: Deuterium-depleted water targets
activities.summary: Drink deuterium-depleted water (DDW — water with less heavy hydrogen than tap water) within these ranges, once location and light are in place.
steps: General range: 25–105 ppm deuterium (tap water is near 150 ppm); 25 ppm water is fine to drink.
Treat 92.5 ppm as the most deuterium a depleted water should carry; go lower if you can afford it, but don't aim for 0 ppm.

Condition-specific targets: 90–105 ppm for GLP-1 drug damage and anorexia; certified under 105 ppm for 90 days for sperm DNA damage; 25–50 ppm for chronic illness; below 100 ppm for movement disorders; below 92 ppm if you live near the SAA. Children: 80–130 ppm.
Buy it (any commercial brand will do; get the lowest ppm you can afford), or make it with zinc and copper electrodes and a small current in a decanter (no voltage or run time is given).
Pair it with carbonated water (see “Carbonated water with DDW”) and with 3% sea salt (see “Sea salt with DDW ("Jade and Salt")”).
Set your own use by your history and response rather than a universal rule.
To check a water's deuterium, send a sample to a water company or chemical lab.
While drinking DDW, also chew hard foods through the day (jerky, seafood, mastic gum).
activities.equipmentDetail: DDW, bought or home-made
activities.cautions: Fix location and light first; DDW comes after them. Feeling worse at first is expected in a deuterium-loaded body and isn't, on its own, a reason to stop.

activities.name: Carbonated water with DDW
activities.summary: Drink carbonated water together with DDW — he treats CO₂ as a diamagnetic quiet-zone around Complex IV when endogenous metabolic CO₂ falls.
steps: Drink carbonated water alongside DDW.
Use plain soda water, or natural sparkling mineral water: Muszynianka (naturally carbonated volcanic spring water, the first choice) or San Pellegrino.
Drink a glass about 15 minutes before a hypnosis session (see “Hypnosis session”).
For mouth-breathing children with dark circles under the eyes, start with carbonated water.
Drink it on flights and in cold settings.
activities.equipmentDetail: carbonated water or a carbonator; DDW
activities.cautions: Trouble tolerating carbonated water is a sign of deeper "lattice lock" (stiff, deuterium-loaded body water).

activities.name: Sea salt with DDW ("Jade and Salt")
activities.summary: Take mineral-rich sea salt (ideally with rare-earth traces) with DDW, while grounded and in the sun; use it to de-frag before hard work — he also frames 92.5 ppm DDW + ~3% salt as a manual “dielectric stator” when the planetary field fades.
steps: Make DDW at 92.5 ppm or lower your base water (see “Deuterium-depleted water targets”).

In about 20 oz (600 ml) of that water, stir roughly one tablespoon of unrefined salt carrying ~70–84 minerals; prefer sources that naturally carry rare-earth traces when you can find them. Clean ocean water diluted to 3% salinity is also fine near the sea.
Drink it before training or other hard demand so the blood vortex can hold deuterium; pee volume falling and urine lightening over weeks are his informal signs it is working.
Optional: a pinch of the same salt in black coffee (cuts cream and bitterness) or on the rim of a drink if you still take alcohol.
Do it alongside barefoot grounding, ideally on basalt, and sun with UV; treat salt, DDW, grounding and UV as one package.
Make it a priority if you carry a tropical maternal lineage (L, M, N, Y) and live somewhere high-declination or low-UV, or while you live in the Southern Hemisphere or near the SAA.
At high latitude with a strong field (around 48°N), keep the salt going alongside daily red/NIR light (see “Sun first, red-light panels second”).
activities.equipmentDetail: unrefined high-mineral sea salt or clean seawater; DDW
activities.cautions: Don't salt-load as a standalone fix while deuterium-loaded and unpinned; it belongs with grounding and a good field. Intravenous 3% saline is a clinician's tool only. People already well-structured may need less salt than those stiff with lattice lock.

activities.name: Wild seafood, DHA and careful iodine
activities.summary: Get DHA, magnesium and antioxidants from wild seafood rather than pills, and keep iodine low unless you are pinned.
steps: Eat wild-caught seafood regularly for DHA (in its natural, un-esterified form) and magnesium. In North America, source from the Pacific: wild sockeye or halibut, or small, short-lived fish such as sardines and anchovies, rather than East Coast oysters.
Take astaxanthin only as food — wild sockeye or krill — ideally after barefoot time in the morning surf.
Limit iodine if you are unpinned, and take no isolated or high-dose iodine supplements.
Take no iodine at all while living in the South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA — a large weak patch in Earth's magnetic field).
Black Sea and Mediterranean seafood is fine for now. Avoid southern-hemisphere and farmed seafood (such as Australian aquaculture), and prefer wild ocean fish to freshwater fish.
For potassium, lean on marine sources: octopus, cuttlefish, wild halibut and salmon, and clams (which add copper).

As the field weakens, eat more cholesterol and DHA — he treats long-chain marine DHA as the membrane "Faraday shield" that seed oils displace, and as a waveguide insulator that supports fluid magnetic vortices.

Eat small oily fish such as sardines and mackerel often, above all in pregnancy and childhood, rather than leaning on lentils or other vegetarian protein — include iodine-rich seafood when pinned; he ties iodine to T3-driven myelin work.
Don't switch to a whole-food plant-based or vegan diet.
activities.cautions: Take antioxidants only in whole marine foods, not pills. Don't use astaxanthin to mask a failing environment — fix light, water and magnetism first. Pair seafood DHA with cutting seed oils (see “Saturated fat as main fuel”). Keep iodine careful if unpinned (step 3).

activities.name: Eat in daylight, nothing after dark
activities.summary: Eat in daylight — a first meal in the morning and the main meal near solar noon — and nothing after dark.
steps: Get sunrise light first, then eat a big first meal rich in protein and fat, near the natural cortisol peak; don't skip it.
Eat the main meal near solar noon, ideally outdoors in real sun.
Keep a sun-timed, seasonal eating schedule.
Eat nothing after dark, zero-carb food included.
Never eat on a plane.

activities.name: Saturated fat as main fuel
activities.summary: Run mainly on saturated fat, keep carbs for full-sun equatorial living, and fix light and location before diet.
steps: Favor saturated fats: grass-fed ghee, coconut oil, lard, tallow, butter, clarified butter.

Skip industrial seed oils (soy, corn, canola, sunflower, safflower and similar linoleic-acid oils); in his model those short omega-6 chains replace marine DHA in the mitochondrial membrane fat cardiolipin and flatten its geometry.
Eat egg yolks for choline.

Eat carbs only if you live near the equator under full UV, and cut them when sun is weak or the field is declining. Eat local fruit only in season and on days of strong sun — never at night or on cloudy or rainy days.
Avoid year-round fructose and never use corn syrup (beet sugar is the lesser harm); in the tropics, also skip local cane sugar and corn products.
Don't use protein as a main fuel: no daily protein powder, and no carnivore diet in the tropics.
As you shift to burning animal fat, notice whether your breathing and mental clarity change.
If a keto flu won't lift, look at your light and magnetic environment, and do deep cold before changing diet further.

Get potassium from greens cooked in fat — beet greens, Swiss chard or spinach with lard, tallow, ghee or butter — plus avocado and salted macadamias or walnuts. Don't rely on potatoes, sweet potatoes or coconut water for it. Keep spinach moderate (no daily raw spinach smoothies) and get iron from red meat.
A model plan for the tropics: Pacific seafood, grass-fed tallow, local lard and butter as the main fuel.
activities.cautions: No diet fixes a location or light problem.

activities.name: Eat food from your own zip code
activities.summary: Eat fresh, seasonal food grown where you live, ideally from your own garden.
steps: Grow or buy food from your own zip code; fresh-picked beats shipped produce displayed under LEDs.
Eat in season and in the light the food grew under — no tropical fruit such as bananas in a northern winter.
Get nutrients from local whole foods eaten in sunlight, not synthetic pills.
Avoid maize-derived (C4) glucose and supplement bases, along with sugar cane, sorghum and high-fructose corn syrup; skip grain from the North American prairies and breadbasket.
Keep deuterium in your daily food low, more strictly the worse your location.
Avoid food and water from weak-shield zones such as the SAA.
Drink alcohol only occasionally, ideally where the local field is stable; where the field has declined, none at all.
In weak-field regions (such as Canada, the UK and SAA areas), build meals on animal fats, green above-ground vegetables and pasture-raised protein.
In the garden, use microbial inoculants, fungi and basalt rock dust rather than synthetic nitrogen.
If a child turns away from higher-deuterium foods, respect the aversion.

activities.name: Coherent dry fast
activities.summary: Dry fast (no food or water) only if you carry enough body fat, grounded in morning sun, and never indoors.
steps: Check you have fat to draw on: not below about 20% body fat if you are in strong sun, and not with a BMI under about 24.
Build your baseline beforehand on saturated fats (ghee, coconut oil, lard, clarified butter).
Fast barefoot and grounded in morning sun.
Add cold exposure if you can.
Break the fast with saturated fat.
activities.cautions: Never fast indoors under LEDs and wireless; fix light and field first. Don't force fat loss by calorie restriction or GLP-1 drugs in a poor light or EMF setting.

activities.name: Barefoot grounding, done right
activities.summary: Stand barefoot on natural, conductive ground every day, especially at dawn, and choose the ground with care.
steps: At dawn, go barefoot in surf, on wet sand, dewy grass, raw soil or basalt, for 20–60 minutes a day; more is fine. On beach days, 2–3 hours at the water's edge, wearing as little as possible, is better still. Be grounded whenever you're in the sun.
At the shore, keep only feet and ankles in the water and as much skin as possible in the air, rather than standing neck-deep.
Prefer basalt or wet volcanic black sand; in a weakening field, choose basalt over any PEMF (pulsed magnetic field) device.
On clay or river-delta ground, stand on raw earth away from concrete slabs.
Don't ground on salt-soaked limestone (karst) near resorts or big power lines, or over oil and gas deposits.
If stray current worries you, check the spot with a meter.
When wiring a ground connection, never join dissimilar metals.
Indoors, use a low-resistance grounding system as the fallback, and sleep grounded (above all with disc problems).
Ground more if you have collagen disease, high ferritin, pale skin or heart-rhythm problems, and before and after athletic training or races.
Where old rock carries a reversed magnetic signature, stand on a normal-polarity basalt flow instead ("directed local grounding").
Swap rubber-soled shoes for leather soles.
activities.equipmentDetail: none (optional meter; indoor grounding system)
activities.cautions: Grass isn't enough where the field is "dead" or declination changes steeply, and grounding alone does little there. Florida and the Yucatán are poor grounding sites during the field decline.

activities.name: Pin first, then light, then exercise and diet
activities.summary: Fix your magnetic and wireless environment first, add morning light second, and only then change exercise or diet — he says sun alone is not enough in a magnetic-forge era; light and grounding belong together.
steps: Leave the wireless "soup": cut nnEMF (man-made electromagnetic fields) at home and work — he links artificial frequencies to leaking calcium channels and lost membrane confinement.
Ground strictly — skin to earth, or a low-resistance indoor grounding system — to flood the body with Earth DC electrons and restore negative cellular voltage.
Sleep in a zero-EMF bedroom.

Add morning solar ultraviolet-A and infrared on bare skin and eyes while grounded (see “Sunrise light on bare eyes and skin”); he treats that pair as rebuilding the water battery at cytochrome c oxidase when oxygen stays paramagnetic.
Only then change exercise or diet.

Fuller version, for the chronically ill and people returning from spaceflight: 30 minutes a day under 660 and 850 nm light before any exercise; nights inside a zero-EMF shield wired to a dedicated ground line; raw bioactive polyphenols; DDW at 25–50 ppm only.
Try to get pinned where you live first; move only if you can't.
activities.equipmentDetail: grounding; optional 660/850 nm panel, bed shielding
activities.cautions: Don't start sick, unpinned people on Zone 2 or HIIT training, supplement stacks, peptides, Cialis or GLP-1 drugs — he treats those exogenous chemicals as rogue "impurities" that trap electrons and dump heat into the mitochondrial network when light and field aren't already stable. High-dose oral vitamin D3 and "longevity" pills do not fix a place locked under steep (vertical) field geometry — change the magnetic environment or relocate first. A sunny vacation alone won't fix low vitamin D if you otherwise live indoors under blue light and wireless.

activities.name: Relocation checklist
activities.summary: How to judge where to live: local magnetic field first, then sun, ground and wireless load, weighed together.
steps: Look up the place in the World Magnetic Model: total intensity above about 45,000 nT (ideally up to 60,000), inclination (how steeply field lines dip) 0–45° so the horizontal component stays strong, declination (compass offset from true north) near 0°. Steep inclination (vertical "Bz" lock) is a reason to leave, not to stack supplements.
Read the declination map: green (the agonic, zero-declination line) is best, red (east) acceptable, dark blue very bad; leave places where the lines bunch together.

Look for an agonic line crossing a volcanic chain at a strong-sun, lower-latitude baseline; prefer iron-rich volcanic / plutonic ground where field lines lie flatter against the crust. Follow agonic lines, not latitude alone.
Compare the town's ESA Swarm (field-mapping satellite) map on the same date across years to see which way it's heading.
Avoid the South Atlantic Anomaly, the Caribbean included.
Check the ground: basalt or wet black sand to stand on; a beach with a good field reading is ideal. Don't buy black sand — live where it occurs naturally.

Before buying land, compare mosquito activity by day and night, burn a 24-hour beeswax candle on site (see “Beeswax candle test”) and study the local water cycle. A nearby volcano wearing a steady cloud cap is a good sign; a bare one in humid country, a bad one.
Avoid places with aurorae, clusters of sick people, dying birds, bees or fish, or surges of old diseases (such as flea-borne typhus in Los Angeles County).
Reject smart houses and live on the ground floor.
Judge all factors together. Don't pick a place for low wireless alone, and don't let mitigation gear talk you into staying somewhere bad.

Places to rule out: California (he cites roughly +11° to +12° east declination off the agonic — enough, in his model, to tip Complexes I–III into a Marcus inversion while UV-B stays too weak to rebuild membrane water), Tennessee, Kansas, deserts (Arizona and South Texas included), northern tech hubs, Colorado, Hawaii, Minnesota, Mexico, the UK, Germany, Portugal and the Azores, continental China and Mongolia, Belgium and Canada; also Australia, New Zealand and the rest of the Southern Hemisphere, Puerto Rico, the Bahamas and Peru. Florida, the Yucatán and coastal Louisiana rate poorly, and the US east of the Rockies is at risk; the Pacific Northwest is the only US option (weigh its offshore volcanic risk). In Asia, look at the Philippines or pinned parts of Japan, or the Hong Kong region if you can accept its crowding.
Move a sick child living at high latitude (around 55°N) somewhere both on an agonic line and at low latitude. Move before starting a family, not after.
Northern lineages should move gradually (see “Four-phase sun day (building a "solar callus")”); until then, use summer light, ground on iron-rich bedrock and use cold.
Before a permanent move, try a two-to-three-month stay in the candidate place when you can, and notice how sleep, energy and clarity change before you uproot fully.
After moving, expect a period of adjustment, possibly feeling worse first. After any de-frag, change the environment too, or the problem returns.
If you already carry a heavy deuterium load, don't stay above about 35° latitude.
activities.equipmentDetail: World Magnetic Model and Swarm maps; beeswax candles
activities.cautions: Your maternal haplogroup (ancestral lineage) sets how much declination you tolerate; for African L lineages 2–4° can matter, and he treats even a few degrees off the agonic as enough to skew Complexes I–III. Agonic lines move with the poles, so recheck — he ties field-line geometry to mitochondrial junction geometry and membrane voltage. Match lineage to circuit: pale / uncoupled northern haplotypes evolved for strong field and low UV struggle under equatorial sun without a melanin shield unless they acclimate (see “Four-phase sun day (building a "solar callus")”); coupled tropical lineages at high latitude lack the winter "internal light" machinery and need strong sun seasons, pinning, or relocation — not oral vitamin D as the fix. Northern lineages historically "outsourced" spin filtering to strong vertical fields after dropping melanin; sun without a stable magnetic forge is incomplete in his model.

activities.name: El Salvador specifics
activities.summary: Practical notes for moving to El Salvador: entry, where to live, land, water and schooling.
steps: For a quick move, contact the relocation attorney through forum member support and use the members-only "Turn Key" route.

Flying in from the US you don't need a return ticket: tell customs you have no fixed departure date and keep your local address at hand; everyone gets 180 days. From Canada, Avianca flies direct from Toronto to San Salvador.
Buy an empty lot and build rather than buying cheap; test the land first with mosquitoes and a beeswax candle.

Favor areas near active volcanoes (the Ilopango area), Comasagua, wooded Palmyra, the higher ground toward Tamanique, Costa del Sol, Shalpa and Punta Mango on the eastern coast; Portofino is solid, but skip the area near Izalco volcano. Elsewhere on the Central American volcanic arc, Guatemala, Costa Rica and Nicaragua also qualify, and Costa Rica and Panama work as do-it-yourself moves. If you look at Honduras instead, only the Pacific side on the Gulf of Fonseca, close to the border volcano.
Ground at sunrise on the Costa del Sol beach; the Astra Beach Club there is a good base. In the dry season, ground on the volcano rather than the beach (the wet season may flip this).
Visit the capital, but don't live there.
Avoid El Zonte and crowded Playa Marcellino because of their wireless load.
Expect grey-sand beaches to be less rocky than black-sand ones.
Skip raw river shellfish, such as oysters from the El Zonte river.
Plan around the rainy season, which runs to about November.
For children, consider "homebeach" schooling.
Source water from a well drilled into the volcanic aquifer and manage your own supply.
To fund the move, nurses can work two-week locum contracts alternating with two weeks there.
At the Costa Real building, take a unit as far to the right as possible when facing the ocean, never on the left side.

activities.name: Track your local field
activities.summary: Keep watching how the magnetic field is changing where you live, and move early if it worsens. Rebuild the plan from current data when charts shift — do not freeze last year’s checklist by habit.
steps: Start with ESA Swarm satellite data, then add USGS, NOAA and NASA sources. For a home readout, build a cheap fluxgate magnetometer (an optically pumped one is better).
Check NOAA declination drift and secular-acceleration ("jerk" — a sudden change in how fast the field is shifting) charts for your zip code, comparing the same date across years.
Watch for unusual blocked weather patterns and track your own HRV.
If your area shows a jerk or turns toward a vertical field, move before official charts catch up.

Watch local animals: herds splintering, dull dry coats near water, grazing shifted to dawn and dusk, changes in crabs, migratory birds (godwits, Arctic terns, albatross), fish and bees — and above all local people. If you see this, switch to deep aquifer water and tighten your light habits.
Track how health outcomes, such as sudden deaths, cluster by zip code as the charts update.

Optional citizen science: pipe-to-soil readings at pipeline cathodic-protection stations (normally about −850 to −1,200 mV) and clamp-on ammeter readings of stray current; wild swings or polarity flips mark ground-current surges.
Signs of a larger shift to watch for: field at 30–50% of the Laschamp collapse, sudden SAA changes, faster pole drift, day-length changes, polar-motion "hooks," ocean heating from below.

Redo your "zip-code balance" monthly: latitude and altitude, local field strength in nT, and maternal haplogroup (inferred from maternal ancestry if untested). When new dynamo or field releases land, re-check steps 1–4 from fundamentals instead of copying last year’s stack by analogy.
activities.equipmentDetail: ESA Swarm, NOAA, USGS and NASA online tools; optional clamp-on ammeter or home magnetometer

activities.name: Beeswax candle test
activities.summary: Burn a rated beeswax candle where you live and compare its burn time with the rating, as a home check of local field quality — he treats a fast burn as the same physics that speeds the body's "metabolic candle."
steps: Buy pure beeswax candles with a stated burn time (24-hour candles work well); never paraffin.
Burn one at home, or on land you're considering, and time it to the end.
On time means normal; faster (a 24-hour candle gone in about 18 hours) means field decline or heavy wireless — he links that ~25% faster burn to roughly a 10% planetary field loss (~2.5× non-linear).
Slower and clean means a strong field; slower with leftover wax means artificial over-clamping, such as from heavy static magnets.
On land, read the result together with day-versus-night mosquito activity.
activities.equipmentDetail: rated pure-beeswax candle
activities.cautions: If the source of disturbance is visibly overhead, the test isn't needed. Don't answer a fast candle with supplement stacks — fix location, grounding and wireless load (see “Pin first, then light, then exercise and diet”).

activities.name: Live low: ground floor, or shield the bed
activities.summary: Live and sleep no higher than the first floor; if you can't move yet, shield and ground the bed.
steps: Choose a home on the ground or first floor.
If you must stay higher for now, build a "High-Altitude Counter-Faraday Shield": conductive mesh around the bed, wired to dedicated ground rods driven into real earth.

Fuller version: vapor-permeable nickel-copper-carbon mesh around sleeping and living spaces, and ground rods at least 30 ft into the water table, kept separate from the utility ground and connected to carbon-fiber sleeping mats.
Alternatively, use copper vortex devices (Slim Spurling coils, Lakhovsky rings) with grounded carbon mats.
Other indoor options: Helmholtz coils giving a pure 21 Hz sine-wave field at about 50 µT, and drinking water distilled at the tap to below 65 ppm deuterium.
activities.equipmentDetail: shielding mesh, ground wire and rods, carbon mats; optional copper vortex devices, Helmholtz coils

activities.name: Cut nnEMF, AC fields first
activities.summary: Reduce nnEMF ("non-native," man-made electromagnetic fields), dealing with low-frequency AC magnetic fields first.
steps: For any chronic problem, first look for AC magnetic fields under 100 kHz (wiring, appliances) and artificial blue light.
Measure before mitigating, ideally with a credentialed assessor; cheap fixes do little.
Don't sleep or live near smart meters, Wi-Fi routers or 5G arrays, or long-term near wind turbines.
Keep phones and earbuds away from head and neck, and phones and laptops off the lap and out of pockets; get rid of smart rings and other radio-emitting wearables.
Use a wired internet connection.
Don't trust airplane mode.
Don't use a phone in the car; buy an older car rather than trying to shield a new one.
Don't install a smart house.
Leave the area when wildfire smoke is heavy.
Skip vibration plates; he rates their RF output worse than a CPAP machine's.
activities.equipmentDetail: optional meter or professional assessment
activities.cautions: Artificial blue light plus wireless noise is especially costly for high-flux / uncoupled northern lineages, who in his model process oxygen fast enough that scrambled fields tilt signaling toward damaging superoxide — strip bedroom and work nnEMF first.

activities.name: Low-EMF, daylit work space
activities.summary: Work in daylight with as few AC magnetic sources nearby as possible.
steps: Move wiring, power supplies and appliances away from where you sit.
Keep the laptop off your lap and the phone out of your pocket.
Open a window for daylight.
Use incandescent rather than LED lighting.
Where you can, choose work that lets you be outdoors and grounded every day.

activities.name: North–south bed
activities.summary: Align the bed along the north–south geomagnetic axis, head to the north.
steps: Find magnetic north with a compass.
Turn the bed so its long axis runs north–south, head at the north end, and give it a full 8-hour night.
Recheck the direction now and then; the magnetic axis is moving.
Add a grounded sheet and a dark, wireless-free room (see “Sleep sanctuary”).
activities.equipmentDetail: compass

activities.name: Magnetic sleep pad (Magnetico) guidance
activities.summary: When a static magnetic sleep pad is worth using, and how to use one.
steps: Choose a high-strength pad giving a steady 10–20 gauss (such as the Magnetico Super Sleep Pad) rather than 5 gauss.
Sleep on it all night — a full 8 hours in field-decline areas — not in short bursts.
During the field decline, use a north-seeking pad, laid with the negative (north) pole facing your body, and pair it with pure DHA and raw morning UV-A.
Lay a grounding sheet on top of the pad.
Switch off Wi-Fi and keep every device away from the pad; if you can't keep tech out of the bedroom, skip the pad.
Children living in a poor magnetic zip code need one.
Don't worry about a pad's dead zone.
Cheap alternative: coil heavy-gauge copper pipe from a hardware store and put it under the pillow.
If you try a different pad, measure the field it gives off and how you respond.

Skip it in El Salvador if you get outside on the volcanic ground. In decline areas, TENS may be the wiser choice (see “Home TENS / vagus protocol”). In the Southern Hemisphere, relocate rather than rely on a pad.
activities.equipmentDetail: static magnetic pad or copper-pipe coil
activities.cautions: A strong vertical field at night and a very different one by day can confuse the brain's sense of direction. Avoid heavy static-magnet jewelry such as magnetic bracelets; wear magnetic necklaces only on flights.

activities.name: Basalt stone and copper ring (passive alternative to TENS)
activities.summary: Current-free alternatives to electrical nerve stimulation: basalt against the skull, copper rings (open or closed), copper–rare-earth jewelry when ungrounded, or a stone in the pillow.
steps: Ground yourself first.
Rest a smooth black basalt stone (or volcanic clay) on the bony ridge behind the ear (occipitomastoid suture) or on the side of the temple (pterion).

At home, wear a plain copper ring about 30 cm (12 in) across around the neck over the vagus nerve or around the head — Lakhovsky-style with ends left unjoined, or a Spurling-style closed coil of copper wire.
When traveling or otherwise ungrounded, wear copper jewelry that also carries a rare-earth magnet (e.g. neodymium) so a static local field travels with you.

Or keep a small paramagnetic (weakly magnet-attracted) stone in the pillow, or hold a piece of green jade (nephrite) shaped to fit the eye socket against the temple while using screens; without jade, wear a 30 cm coiled copper necklace.
For head pressure and nausea, use the neck ring in place of a vagus stimulator.
For blood sugar, place Spurling or Lakhovsky copper rings over the neck's vagal "choke point" and the solar plexus.
At home scale: build with, or line living spaces with, local basalt or volcanic stone; don't import basalt sand into a home with no tie to the regional field.
activities.equipmentDetail: black basalt stone or volcanic clay; 30 cm copper ring (open or closed); optional copper–neodymium necklace; optional jade (nephrite)
activities.cautions: A bridge while you fix your location, not a substitute for volcanic ground. Jump conduction from nearby wireless is a real worry; still prefer the jewelry on planes over flying bare.

activities.name: Flying and travel
activities.summary: Fly as little as possible; treat jet lag as a short magnetic excursion and limit the harm when you must fly — he says weak-field, high-wireless cities make subjective time feel faster until you re-pin.
steps: Skip unneeded flights, especially circumpolar routes and long east–west ones over the Atlantic and the SAA.

When seriously ill, heal locally first rather than flying to treatment. Don't fly with a headache or other acute illness if you're already deuterium-loaded, and de-frag a sick person locally before putting them on a plane.
Never eat on a plane; drink carbonated water instead (short-term magnetic-flux offset, not a long-term fix).
In flight, wear copper–rare-earth (or other static magnetic) jewelry — he treats this as mandatory once you leave the ground, not optional fashion.
Expect muscle loss after flights or time at altitude.
Cut ungrounded travel generally — tech-dense or SAA-adjacent coasts (his Gulf / New Orleans example) can collapse sleep and voltage within days; return to a pinned tropical volcanic site to recover.
Time trips abroad to coincide with your home's darkening season.
Avoid cruise ships whose routes cross the SAA.
activities.equipmentDetail: copper–rare-earth or static magnetic necklace for flights; carbonated water
activities.cautions: Don't fight travel "time speeding up" with longevity peptides or thyroid-rate pills; re-ground at sunrise and get full-spectrum morning light instead (“Sunrise light on bare eyes and skin”, “Barefoot grounding, done right”).

activities.name: Space-weather days
activities.summary: On days of strong solar or geomagnetic activity, ground longer than usual and keep strict morning habits.
steps: Watch forecasts for M- and X-class solar flares and geomagnetic storms; brace for the 48 hours after big flares.
Ground longer than your usual 20–60 minutes on storm days.
Be extra strict about morning sun during strong ground-current surges.
Expect possible headaches, pressure in the head, sleep disruption or circadian "off" days when the field is noisy — treat them as space weather, not a cue to start new pills.
If clear, high-radiation days bring fatigue or word-finding stumbles, have a dark, cool room to retreat to.
activities.cautions: Do not answer a storm with high-dose oral vitamin D or supplement stacks; lengthen grounding and keep morning light instead.

activities.name: Air-tube headphones, never Bluetooth
activities.summary: Listen through wired, shielded air-tube headphones or a speaker, never Bluetooth.
steps: For all audio, including sound routines, use air-tube headphones or a room speaker.
Never use Bluetooth headphones or AirPods.
Keep phones and earbuds off the head and neck, above all if you have a dry mouth.
activities.equipmentDetail: air-tube headphones or speaker

activities.name: Live outdoors, not as an "astronaut on Earth"
activities.summary: Spend your days outdoors on real ground, and raise children the same way.
steps: Move as much of daily life outdoors as you can.
Take slow walks among green plants and trees.
Give children unfiltered morning UV-A and infrared on eyes and skin, bare feet on the earth, and a home without Wi-Fi or artificial night light.
Give babies morning and late-afternoon sun for 2–4 weeks, then unrestricted sun; a newborn should see the sun while grounded.
Don't raise children in deserts or indoors as "astronauts on Earth."
Choose dim outdoor light over bright indoor light.

activities.name: Sleep sanctuary
activities.summary: Make the bedroom cold, totally dark, grounded and wireless-free — he treats sleep as the body's nightly deuterium-clearing Hall-current / polarity flip, not only rest.
steps: Switch off Wi-Fi, routers and all wireless devices before sleep, and keep devices out of the room. Turning off the bedroom's breaker at night helps too; also check the spot for geopathic stress.
Turn the lights off at a reasonable hour and make the room totally dark — no screens; night blue undoes the day's retinal clock charge.
Keep the room cold; in his model a small overnight drop in brain/CSF temperature helps shrink respiratory-complex spacing so heavy hydrogen is cleared.
Sleep on a grounded sheet; no electric (adjustable) bed.
Align the bed north–south (see “North–south bed”).

Earn the night with full morning and midday outdoor light (“Sunrise light on bare eyes and skin”, “Midday sun and UV-B, unfiltered”); he says solar UV-B/VDR prep during the day is what lets sleep finish the purge.
activities.equipmentDetail: grounded sheet; blackout
activities.cautions: When sleep won't come, avoid sleeping pills, melatonin supplements and Bluetooth sleep trackers, Oura-type rings included; for persistent sleep problems, look at relocation and nnEMF rather than pills or machine pressure alone (he rates CPAP as missing the field/light cause). Indoor Faraday living (concrete/steel/wireless) mimics a magnetic decline in his model.

activities.name: Cold thermogenesis
activities.summary: Use daily cold exposure, more where sun is weak or the field poor, plus targeted ice on the head and neck — he treats cold as a deuterium sieve that helps sustain wakefulness.
steps: If you're new to it, add cold gradually, at sunrise or after sunset, keeping it a couple of hours apart from your last meal; not everyone needs it.

Simplest daily option: each morning, 60–180 seconds of cold water on bare skin, cold enough that you want to get out but still safe (about 14 °C/57 °F) — a cold shower or plunge, or, if your heart is healthy, face dunking or an ice pack on face and neck. Northern lineages (such as H) at high latitude: a morning cold-water splash.

Use whole-body cold in winter, at high latitude, and wherever sun is poor or the field weak or skewed. Northern lineages (H, J, T, U, K) living in high-UV or high-radiation zones should be strict about it.
Do deep cold before attempting diet changes, and use plenty of cold and grounding while losing fat.
In the tropics, swimming in natural water counts, and so does free-diving in cold water (see “Swim and soak in natural water”).
At dawn, don't let cold compete with light: feet in the surf, body in the air.
Targeted cold: ice on the roof of the mouth, under the chin or on the back of the neck. Chewing ice cools the teeth too.
Wear a compression shirt during cold sessions.
Sun first, cold afterwards. For a painful joint, put sun on it and then cold on that same joint.

Pair cold with UV-B daytime sun (see “Midday sun and UV-B, unfiltered”): in his model cold shrinks the spacing between respiratory complexes so heavy hydrogen is filtered, and solar UV-B/VDR keeps the membrane out of a Marcus jam so waking energy holds.
activities.equipmentDetail: cold water (shower, tub, sea, lake); ice packs; optional compression shirt
activities.cautions: East and Southeast Asian maternal lineages (D5b1, F) in a weak field should skip deep cold (55–65 °F) until pinned, first maximizing morning light, grounding and nnEMF shielding. In a high-declination zone such as California he treats deep cold as a short bridge only — not a sustainable stand-in for relocating to flatter field geometry (see “Relocation checklist”). An ice face dunk before sleep may calm you or wire you, depending on how deuterium-loaded you are; clear deuterium first. Cold-and-dark alone is not a license to skip sleep or morning light.

activities.name: Swim and soak in natural water
activities.summary: Swim in the sea or other natural water rather than chlorinated pools, let children swim in sunlight without goggles, and take warmth from geothermal water.
steps: Swim in daylight in the ocean, a lake or other natural water.
Stay out of chlorinated pools; if you use a pool, pick a saltwater one.
Let children swim in the sun without goggles, so the light reaches their eyes.
Before and after an ocean swim, do jumping jacks on the beach.
Learn free-diving, cold water included, and get scuba-certified.
For warmth outdoors, use a geothermal hot spring instead of a patio heater; for sauna heat, prefer a geothermal sauna or a temazcal (traditional sweat lodge).

activities.name: Exercise, environment first
activities.summary: De-frag first, then move daily outdoors and grounded at moderate intensity — environment first, fitness second.
steps: Before hard sessions, assume you are deuterium-loaded: ground barefoot (no rubber soles), drink mineral salt water (see “Sea salt with DDW ("Jade and Salt")”), consider castor oil in the navel (see “Castor oil in the navel”) or gentle left-ear vagus work, and only then train.

Move every day in ways that drive blood, lymph and spinal-fluid flow; favor mechanical and gravitational loading. He frames exercise as an electromagnetic event whose job is to keep deuterium in the blood and the head's vortex spinning.
Mix aerobic intervals (such as uphill sprints) with steady effort, and keep strength work slow and controlled, without breath-holding or straining.

Train outdoors and grounded; avoid blue-lit gyms, especially when unwell. During the field decline, don't train indoors; sealed, crowded gyms can reach 1,500 ppm CO₂ or more, against about 415 ppm outdoors.
Don't go straight from screens into a workout.
Don't spend years running ungrounded in rubber-soled shoes.
Keep intensity moderate; don't overtrain. Don't shred large fat stores until light, grounding and arterial melanin can hold the released deuterium.
Don't assume hard competitive exercise protects you, and don't make building muscle a goal in old age.
If you must use a gym, choose one with open doors or windows, go at quiet hours, carry a portable CO₂ monitor, and get fresh air afterwards.
Through the day, walk and talk outdoors in daylight rather than sitting for long stretches, silent, under artificial light.
activities.equipmentDetail: none (optional portable CO₂ monitor)
activities.cautions: Exercise, and compression machines like Vasper, can do harm when you are deuterium-loaded or unpinned; pin first (see “Pin first, then light, then exercise and diet”), and de-frag before training if you're lattice-locked. Don't push to your limit in a weak field without grounding. On GLP-1 drugs, even moderate exercise acts like overtraining.

activities.name: Home TENS / vagus protocol
activities.summary: Settings and placements for gentle TENS (a skin-electrode nerve stimulator) on the vagus nerve or upper abdomen.
steps: Use a unit with a biphasic, net-zero-charge waveform (not constant DC).
Placement A: ear clip on the left tragus or concha (where the vagus branches into the ear), return pad on the same side's occipitomastoid suture (the bony ridge behind the ear).
Placement B: pads on the solar plexus (upper abdomen) and on the T10–T12 muscles beside the spine.
Polarity: black negative lead nearest the target nerve, red positive lead farther away.
Frequency: a constant 25 Hz (stay within 20–25 Hz; 40 Hz is for brain-wave work, not vagal TENS).
Pulse width: 200–250 µs, no wider.
Intensity: 0.5–2.0 mA, below sensation or a faint tingle — never twitching or pain.
Session: 15–30 minutes, once or twice a day.
Children: no fixed settings; find them by trial and error, ideally with someone monitoring the child's HRV during sessions.
activities.equipmentDetail: biphasic TENS unit; ear-clip electrode; pads
activities.cautions: Left side only: never the right ear or right side of the neck, whose vagus branch drives the heart's pacemaker (risk of a dangerously slow beat or arrest). No pads to the left of the larynx or at the base of the neck; avoid the temple (pterion); never run it for hours. For a current-free option, see “Basalt stone and copper ring (passive alternative to TENS)”.

activities.name: Vagal toning with voice and sound
activities.summary: Tone the vagus nerve daily with slow breathing, humming, gargling, massage, falling water and resonant sound.
steps: Slow belly breathing, the main daily practice: in through the nose for 4 seconds, out gently for 8 seconds, for 5–10 minutes.

Hum, chant "OM" or sing long tones on the exhale (about 4 s in, 6–8 s out). Before bed, hum, tone, throat-sing (Mongolian style) or strike a frame drum or gong; prefer live sources (voice, gongs, Himalayan bowls) to digital speakers and subwoofers.
Hum a low, buzzing "M" pitched toward 40 Hz so the skull vibrates; best outdoors at sunrise, ideally on volcanic ground (see “Volcano Protocol”).
Gargle hard in 30–60 second bouts, once or twice a day.
Massage the outer ears (rub and pull), head, neck and feet, and rub the eyes firmly for 10–20 seconds.
Do slow, pain-free neck movements ("vagus flossing"), guided at first if you have neck problems.
Try ujjayi ("ocean") breathing at a 1:2 in-to-out ratio, and mild inversions such as legs up the wall, with care if you have blood- or eye-pressure problems.
Laugh, sing and talk loudly every day, and listen to falling water.
Use resonant rooms or tones near 110 Hz, real instruments tuned to 432 Hz and nature sounds, and cut digital background noise.
In the evening, put a 128 Hz fork on the sternum or neck (see “Tuning forks: 128 Hz and 40 Hz”).
Pound your chest as often as you like.
Clear the ears with a closed-throat pressure "snap," the way you pop them on a plane.
activities.equipmentDetail: none (optional 128 Hz fork; frame drum, gong or singing bowl)

activities.name: Castor oil in the navel
activities.summary: Put castor oil in the navel to tone the vagus via the falciform remnant — nightly, or a few times a day before hard demand.
steps: Buy organic, cold-pressed, hexane-free castor oil.
Put 3–5 drops directly into the navel (he treats the navel scar and falciform ligament as a dense vagal pathway).
At night, leave it in overnight; before training, 2–3 daytime applications are fine as a powerless pre-workout de-frag.
Pair it with sunrise light, grounding and DDW in the same routine.
activities.equipmentDetail: organic cold-pressed, hexane-free castor oil
activities.cautions: Use castor oil rather than DMSO.

activities.name: Tuning forks: 128 Hz and 40 Hz
activities.summary: Use a 128 Hz fork on stiff or nerve areas and in the evening, and a 40 Hz fork in the morning and at lunch.
steps: Strike the fork and press its stem against the body.
For pain or stiffness: 128 Hz on stiff joints (such as ankles), along the sciatic nerve or along the vagal path.
Evening: 128 Hz on the sternum or neck to calm down before sleep.
Morning and lunch: 40 Hz for focus and mood.
The 40 Hz fork also goes on the spine (see “Volcano Protocol”) and the hard palate (see “Mastic gum and palate reset”).
On the sternum, any fork from 40 to 256 Hz works, and so do Tibetan singing bowls.
Place the 40 Hz fork under the back of the skull, in the sub-occipital hollow over the fourth ventricle.
For bone-conduction hearing loss, use forks on the bones around the ear; tai chi on the beach is a fork-free alternative.
Other 40 Hz sources: a hummed "M" (see “Vagal toning with voice and sound”), big drums such as Japanese taiko, or 40 Hz audio played through a speaker.
activities.equipmentDetail: 128 Hz and 40 Hz tuning forks

activities.name: Binaural sleep glide
activities.summary: Play theta, then delta, binaural beats before and while falling asleep.
steps: About 20 minutes before bed, play theta beats (4–7 Hz).
While falling asleep, switch to pure delta (0.5–3.5 Hz).
Optionally add 528 or 432 Hz tones to the wind-down.
Play it through air-tube headphones or a speaker in a dark, tech-free bedroom; never Bluetooth.
activities.equipmentDetail: binaural audio; air-tube headphones or speaker

activities.name: Mastic gum and palate reset
activities.summary: Chew mastic gum daily, the first step for a blocked nose, pair it with a 40 Hz fork on the palate, and scrape the tongue with copper each morning.
steps: Get real mastic gum, not falim gum. For the gums themselves, use the hard resin.
Chew it daily for long stretches, more on the right side than the left; don't swallow it.
For chronic congestion, start here, stop mouth breathing, and ground in morning sun.
Palate reset: while chewing, press a 40 Hz fork's stem against the hard palate toward the sphenoid (the bone behind the nose); pair it with the spinal water jet (see “Volcano Protocol”).
For night-time breathing trouble, chew it for two weeks before turning to a breathing machine, and skip the machine if it works; prefer this to static mouthguards.
Also use it for parotid (salivary) gland problems, and chew it before surgery.
If chewing feels worse at first, keep chewing.
Gagging is another way to stimulate the palate.
Chew hard foods as well, such as jerky and seafood. Skip jaw-trainer gadgets such as Jawzrsize.
Every morning, scrape the tongue with a copper scraper (not steel or plastic): start as far back toward the root as you can and use firm, steady pulls.
Add face exercises that widen the upper jaw sideways (lateral maxillary expansion).
activities.equipmentDetail: mastic gum; 40 Hz tuning fork; copper tongue scraper

activities.name: Sinus-clearing routine
activities.summary: A four-part routine for a blocked sinus or hay fever: humming, positioning, CO₂ breathing and morning grounding.
steps: Sit upright with your mouth shut, breathe in through the nose, then hum low ("OM" or "MMMM") on each exhale, aiming the vibration at the blocked side, for 5–10 minutes.
Lie on the opposite side so the blocked side faces up, head tilted about 45° down, for 5–7 minutes of slow, quiet nasal breathing.

Do 5 minutes of CO₂-retention breathing: small silent breath in and out, pinch the nose for 3–5 seconds, then 10 seconds of gentle nasal breathing; repeat (see “Buteyko under-breathing and sauna CO₂”).
Away from routers and screens, stand barefoot on wet grass, wet sand or in the surf for 20–30 minutes in morning sun.
Athletes: ground heavily before and after every race or practice.
activities.cautions: If congestion keeps coming back, look at your location.

activities.name: Nasal and alternate-nostril breathing
activities.summary: Breathe through the nose day and night, with alternate-nostril breathing and breath holds — he treats nasal nitric oxide as a paramagnetic shield that mouth breathing drops.
steps: Stop mouth breathing: lips closed, breathing through the nose day and night; tape the mouth at night.
Practice alternate-nostril breathing.
Add breath holds and track your breath-hold (BOLT) score.
Mouth-breathing children (dark circles under the eyes are a sign): start with carbonated water, retrain nose breathing with the tongue resting on the palate, and give mastic gum.
activities.cautions: Chronic congestion and a lost sun-sneeze reflex are early warning signs. Think twice about septum surgery.

activities.name: Rhythmic CO₂ pulses (Ryman protocol)
activities.summary: Alternate normal air and CO₂-enriched air every 35 seconds for 30 minutes.
steps: Set up a source of CO₂-raised air.
Switch between room air and the CO₂-raised air every 35 seconds.
Keep the cycle going for 30 minutes.
For an everyday version, drink carbonated water (see “Carbonated water with DDW”).
activities.equipmentDetail: a CO₂-enriched air source (no specific device is named)

activities.name: Buteyko under-breathing and sauna CO₂
activities.summary: Raise carbon dioxide gently by breathing less to lift magnetic flux; pair with cold; use a traditional sauna.
steps: Cut breathing volume: light, slow, quiet nasal breaths.
Aim for arterial CO₂ of about 40–45 mmHg while oxygen saturation stays normal.
Short daily drill: a small breath in and out, a 3–5 second nose-pinch hold, then 10 seconds of easy breathing; repeat for 5 minutes.
In Tummo-style breathing, remember that the breath hold, not the active phase, raises CO₂.
Prefer this under-breathing over hard hyperventilation styles that dump CO₂; pair Buteyko with cold thermogenesis when you use cold.
Optional: train the diaphragm with brass or wind instruments for hypoxia tolerance.
Use a traditional sauna, paired with carbonated water and DDW.
While asleep, wear a Buteyko breathing belt to slow breathing.
activities.equipmentDetail: none (optional pulse oximeter; traditional sauna; Buteyko belt)
activities.cautions: Oxygen saturation must not fall. Cold and sauna can work against each other if misused.

activities.name: Shoreline sunrise wave breathing
activities.summary: Breathe breaking-wave spray at the shoreline each morning at sunrise.
steps: Go to the surf line at sunrise.
Breathe the spray of the breaking waves, and swim in the ocean every morning if you can.
Combine it with sunrise light on bare eyes and skin.
No beach? Breathe beside a waterfall or other falling water; at home, water run down a stepped wall does the same.
Any net negative-ion exposure counts; there's no minimum dose.
Spend less time in ion-poor indoor air, above all with lung fibrosis.

activities.name: Volcano Protocol
activities.summary: A combined routine for spinal "lattice lock": water jet and 40 Hz fork on the spine, carbonated water with DDW, sauna, and sunrise grounding on volcanic ground.
steps: Live or stay somewhere pinned and low-latitude on the Pacific Rim.
Aim a high-power water jet at the mid and lower back (thoracic spine, T5–T12).
At the same time, press a 40 Hz fork to the spine.
Drink carbonated water with DDW.
Use a traditional sauna.
Stand barefoot on volcanic ground at sunrise for UV-A (380 nm) and solar infrared; a volcanic crater at sunrise is best. While there, hum a low "M" near 40 Hz.
Add shoreline wave breathing and the mastic gum palate reset.
Add cold, done while grounded, and deep-tissue massage.
Avoid long east–west flights.
Keep at it long term and track deep-sleep HRV.
activities.equipmentDetail: high-pressure water jet; 40 Hz fork; carbonated water; DDW; sauna
activities.cautions: Distrust anyone who promises a reversal timeline.

activities.name: Hypnosis session
activities.summary: Use hypnosis or self-hypnosis as a "de-frag" session, set up with water and grounding and followed by the fork and water jet.
steps: Learn hypnosis or self-hypnosis (or deep autogenic training).
About 15 minutes before a session, drink a glass of DDW or carbonated water.
Do the session grounded, ideally in a pinned place, with slow belly breathing.
Straight after, while still deeply relaxed, apply the 40 Hz fork and water jet (see “Volcano Protocol”).
activities.equipmentDetail: DDW or carbonated water; 40 Hz fork; water jet

activities.name: HRV and personal scorecard
activities.summary: Track heart-rate variability (HRV — the beat-to-beat variation in heart timing), above all in deep sleep, plus a few simple markers and a daily journal.
steps: Track HRV during deep sleep as your main progress gauge; flexible, rising HRV is the goal.
Treat rigid, flat HRV as a warning sign of lattice lock; chronic congestion and a lost sun-sneeze reflex are others.
Check HRV if you have muscle twitching.
Keep a daily journal of your routine and symptoms, and reread it after 1–3 months and again after 12 months.

Track everyday markers: morning blood sugar, LDL, B12, basal body temperature, hs-CRP, the morning cortisol rise on waking, and new pigment changes; treat high ferritin and fast-shifting potassium as warnings — he reads a rapidly changing potassium as a magnetic/agonic signal (field moving or tracking ruined), not only a diet issue. A BUN-to-creatinine ratio near 10 is good and above 20 a warning; vitamin D of 40–60 ng/mL with low serum calcium is the aim, and D above 100 with high calcium a red flag.

For a wider view: homocysteine, vitamin D, hormone panels, TMAO, MRI white-matter findings and thermography — not your tan. With thermography, scan the face and calves for cold spots and hot inflammatory plumes, and read facial and body heat patterns as a gauge of how thick the blood is running.
Advanced markers: salivary D/H (deuterium ratio) under 130 ppm, quiet and coherent ultra-weak light emission from the body, and nerve DC voltage back near −90 mV.
Optional location readout: a mitochondrial enzyme (OXPHOS) test or an electron-microscopy muscle biopsy.
Score each night on six signs: dry versus puffy, sharp versus foggy vision, dark first urine, a morning HRV surge, warm core with cool skin, and waking with insights.
If you live near a big river or lake, see whether focus and sleep markers (such as morning dryness) shift with distance from the water.
activities.equipmentDetail: HRV monitor; optional thermography
activities.cautions: During a field decline he treats Horvath epigenetic clocks, saliva telomere tests, deuterium breath tests and anti-aging peptides such as Epitalon as distorted — the nucleus, in his model, is blind to mitochondrial timing packets. Don't rely on HRV alone while exercising in a declining zone.

activities.name: Slow time down with novelty
activities.summary: Counter the sense that time is speeding up with novelty, reflection and slow breathing in the sun.
steps: Add novelty: new routes, hobbies, learning.
Journal or practice mindfulness.
Breathe slowly and deeply, ideally standing in morning sun with bare skin ("standing in the light, breathing in the time").
For prayer or intention: ground first, cut nearby EMF, and avoid fluorescent light.

activities.name: Lavender, eucalyptus and chili with humming
activities.summary: Pair the hummed "M" with scent and spice — lavender, eucalyptus and hot pepper — and finish with ice.
steps: While humming "M" (see “Vagal toning with voice and sound”), breathe in lavender, or wear a lavender patch.
Eucalyptus: inhale it while you hum, or rub it on the neck over the vagus; he uses it in place of a cold plunge.
Chili heat: eat spicy food, take a hot-pepper tincture (such as Carolina Reaper or Pepper X; no amount given), or rub capsaicin cream on the belly, the mid-face or over the vagus.
At the peak of the heat, hum "M" and chew ice.
For a hot–cold contrast, use capsaicin on the belly and eucalyptus on the neck in the same session.
activities.equipmentDetail: lavender oil or patch; eucalyptus oil; hot-pepper tincture or capsaicin cream; ice
activities.cautions: If your skin is deuterium-loaded, be wary of acupuncture; he says it can leave you worse.

activities.name: Hair: no dye, no bleach, keep it long
activities.summary: Leave hair its natural color and length: no dye, bleach or henna, and no habit of cutting it short.
steps: Don't dye or bleach your hair, and don't switch to henna (lawsone) as a "natural" substitute.
Don't bleach skin or teeth either.
Wear your hair long rather than cutting it short.
If your hair is already bleached, let it grow out rather than cutting the bleached part off.
Skip hair removal by laser, waxing or plucking.
activities.cautions: Dyes and bleach matter most for women and for anyone living under LED light.

activities.name: Morning bowel movement and stool check
activities.summary: Let the bowel movement follow sunrise and breakfast, go squatting or upright, and read your stool on the Bristol chart each day.
steps: Get sunrise light, then eat your first meal (see “Eat in daylight, nothing after dark”); the morning bowel movement should follow.
Go in an upright position — squatting, or standing as upright as you can — so gravity helps.
Aim for Bristol type 4: a smooth, well-formed sausage that needs little wiping.
Treat loose stools (types 5–7) and hard lumps (types 1–2) as a sign your light, water or field needs work.
Don't hold in gas; floating stools and passing wind are normal.
Skip vegan diets.

articles.title: Mitochondria as light- and field-driven electronics
articles.summary: Kruse treats each mitochondrion as an antenna, circuit and particle accelerator tuned by sunlight and Earth's magnetic field, turning energy into form through resistance rather than simply burning food.
keyPoints: Kruse says mitochondria are not furnaces but electronics: antennas and circuits tuned to sunlight and Earth's magnetic field.
In his model, electron flow depends on spin and the shape of the surrounding field, not only on energy.
He argues energy is never produced, only transformed through resistance, and health sits in a just-right zone of it.
He sees the body's mitochondria as one wired network whose roots go back to iron–sulfur devices older than genes.
In his view this is a hardware problem set by the environment, restored by sunlight, grounding and a stable magnetic field.

sections.body: Textbooks picture mitochondria, the tiny power units inside our cells, as furnaces that burn food. Kruse argues they are better understood as electronics: antennas and circuits tuned to sunlight and to Earth's magnetic field. In his model, whether this circuit works decides almost everything else, from the state of the cell's water to how it handles oxygen.

sections.heading: The Sun's receiver
sections.body:
Kruse calls the link between the mitochondrion and the Sun "Optico-Magnetic Engineering." In his view both are low-energy "quantum synchrotrons" whose output depends on tunneling, the quantum trick by which a particle slips through an energy barrier it could not climb over. In the Sun, hydrogen nuclei tunnel to fuse; in the cell, electrons tunnel between the complexes of the respiratory chain. He therefore sees the mitochondrion as a wireless receiver tuned to the Sun–Earth circuit, and frames health as a shift from "eating mass" to "harvesting flux."

He names one band of sunlight as the receiver's ignition switch. Short-wave infrared near 1878 nanometers carries 0.66 electron-volts, which he gives as the exact kick cytochrome c oxidase, the last enzyme of the electron chain, needs to finish turning oxygen into water. LED lighting spikes in the blue but offers almost nothing in this range. Indoors, in his account, the enzyme slows, less deuterium-poor water gets made, and the cell is short of breath at the quantum level.

He sums up his thesis as two established ideas joined together: conservation of angular momentum (spin cannot simply appear or vanish) and Rudolph Marcus's theory of how fast electrons jump between molecules. Electron flow, in his account, depends on spin and on the shape of the surrounding field.

The link between the two is CISS, chiral-induced spin selectivity. Kruse explains that proteins built with one "handedness" act as spin filters, letting through electrons that spin one way. Earth's field keeps this filter aligned, an effect he calls the "Zeeman handshake." Borrowing the radical-pair idea from bird navigation, he says a weak field does not force a reaction; it tips the balance between spin states, and the cell amplifies the nudge. Change where you live magnetically, he argues, and your chemistry changes without any chemical being added.

sections.heading: The parts as circuit components
sections.body:
Kruse describes the inner membrane as carrying roughly 30 million volts per meter, about 150 millivolts held across a membrane only 4 to 5 nanometers thick, which he likens to a lightning bolt. Cardiolipin, a cone-shaped fat in that membrane, is the insulating sleeve that keeps the respiratory complexes within the 14-ångström tunneling limit he credits to Dutton.

By ordinary standards, he says, that field should spark straight through. The membrane survives because cytochrome c oxidase coats it in structured water low in deuterium (heavy hydrogen), which insulates far better than ordinary water. A single deuterium nucleus touching that field would, in his account, bridge it and cause an "isotopic flashover."

At the tips of the cristae, the membrane's inward folds, cardiolipin gathers negative charge. In his model this focuses a wave of protons the way the undersea canyon at Nazaré, Portugal, focuses ocean swells into giant waves. He calls it the "Biological Nazaré" and says it drives ATP synthase, the rotary motor that makes the cell's energy currency, toward 9,000 revolutions per minute. That makes the mitochondrion, for Kruse, less a power plant than a particle accelerator.

The membrane itself moves. Kruse describes it as piezoelectric, shifting from a loose liquid into an ordered liquid crystal as charge builds, which pulls the enzymes open so electrons can tunnel through. He calls this "unfurling" and likens it to sails: furled sails tear in a gust, unfurled ones harvest it. He sums it up as "metabolism is geometry."

He builds this picture on Albert Szent-Györgyi's 1941 proposal that proteins are semiconductors, John Bardeen's transistor, and Robert O. Becker's map of the body's direct-current signals. In it, cristae act as transistors, and foreign chemicals are "rogue dopants" that trap electrons.

sections.heading: Two kinds of resistance
sections.body:
Kruse says the circuit needs two opposite properties at once. The membrane must insulate well, like a capacitor holding charge, while the electron chain must conduct easily, like a wire. He maps this onto Martin Picard's "energy resistance" idea: health sits in a just-right zone with enough resistance to turn electron flow into useful work, but not so much that energy is wasted as heat.

Energy, in his view, is never produced, only transformed, and always through resistance; with none there would be no work, no information and no life. The 0.66 eV barrier at cytochrome c oxidase is the resistor that brakes incoming solar energy, and that braking builds the membrane's field. That, he says, is why mitochondria are about 10,000 times more energy-dense than the Sun. On this view DNA is a ledger of resistances that worked in the past, and a body's shape is energy turned into form.

Harms come in two matching kinds. Some jam the wire: loss of the magnetic anchor, nnEMF (his term for man-made wireless and electrical fields), light at night, and deuterium, heavy metals and calcium acting as electron traps. Others short the capacitor, including the heat released when the wire jams, which melts the membrane's structured water.

sections.heading: One network, ancient roots
sections.body:
Kruse says mitochondria are one wired network, not isolated units. The junctions between them act as a "bus bar," a shared power rail, so a failure in one tissue spreads body-wide. Citing Martin Picard's images, he adds that cristae line up across neighboring organelles at inner-mitochondrial junctions, letting protons flow coherently through the grid. Healthy cristae, in his reading, follow a brachistochrone — the least-time curve from Complex I to oxygen — and that least-time path is his synonym for longevity; a magnetic field holds the geometry, while a declining one warps it. The network also gives off light: he reads the faint glow every person emits, strongest on the face and peaking in the afternoon, as an organized signal — coherent when electron spins run parallel, incoherent when they do not — which is why he calls the organelle a quantum synchrotron tuned to Earth's field.

He traces this design to life's origins. Building on Lynn Margulis's account of mitochondria as once free-living bacteria, he argues they are photosynthesis machinery run in reverse, and that life began as a solid-state iron–sulfur device for shedding an unshielded early Sun's energy. The merger that made complex cells was a "chiral handshake" of shared handedness; when the field shifts, he says, the handshake slips and cristae alignment is the first thing lost.

In practice, Kruse concludes that this is a hardware problem set by the environment. He says the circuit is restored by full-spectrum sunlight, grounding and a stable local magnetic field, rather than by adding chemicals that in his model only add more electron traps. Daylight matters because LED rooms lack the 1878-nanometer infrared that switches on the last step of the chain. He describes the shift he wants as moving "from the pharmacy to the foundry": shaping the spaces where this hardware works.

terms: From the pharmacy to the foundry

articles.title: The field, the genes and the clock in the cell
articles.summary: In his model the environment sets the physics, the physics sets how genes behave, and DNA carries physical "mass" that light and the daily clock must keep low.
keyPoints: Kruse says the environment comes first: light, magnetism and water set the cell's physics, and that physics decides how genes behave.
In his model the genome is a passive "fab plant" that builds to order, not the programmer of the body.
He reads telomeres as a record of accumulated disorder, shortening when electrons drain away and lengthening when they are plentiful.
He says the daily clock "time-stamps" protein tags and, at night, clears deuterium-laden methyl groups from DNA.
In practice he says to reset the physical environment with grounding, full sun, a horizontal magnetic field and dark nights.

sections.body: Kruse turns the usual view of genes as the body's blueprint upside down. In his model the environment comes first: it sets the physics inside the cell, and that physics decides how genes behave. This matters to him because it means gene tests and "biological age" clocks measure late effects, while the causes lie in light, magnetism and water.

sections.heading: Environment first, genes last
sections.body:
Kruse reads Nature's 2024 essay arguing that genes are not the blueprint for life as mainstream biology catching up with him, though he says it still misses the real cause: deuterium (heavy hydrogen) and the physics of the cell's water. In his view the nuclear genome is a passive library, and the slow drift of chemical marks on DNA (epigenetic drift) simply follows damage done by the field.

He spells out his own chain of command. Light picks the physical rules a cell runs under, melanin is the hardware, proteins are the product, and the genome is the "fab plant," the chip factory that builds to order rather than the programmer who writes the design. Raise someone under artificial light and the result, in his view, is a mismatch of frequencies, not a genetic error.

He finds a vivid example in Lydia Fairchild, who had absorbed a twin in the womb and so carried two genetically distinct cell lines. Kruse calls her a "nuclear chimera but mitochondrial monolith": both lines ran on the same maternal mitochondria, so her body stayed coherent. For him the case shows that the self is defined by the mitochondrial field, with the nucleus a secondary parts library.

He stresses that DNA is paramagnetic (weakly drawn to a magnet) when wet, though not when dry. Gene activity, he says, therefore follows the strength and direction of the surrounding magnetic field, which he calls "electromagnetic terroir." In his telling, ancient peoples sheltered in paramagnetic stone when the field weakened.

sections.heading: Telomeres as a record of disorder
sections.body:
Telomeres are the protective caps on the ends of chromosomes. Kruse adopts the TRCS (Telomere/rDNA Co-Regulation) model, from a 2026 paper he credits to Huang. It holds that the physical shortening of telomeres and other repeated DNA stretches drives cell aging by raising p53, the protein that guards the genome. Epigenetic drift is only a passenger, which he says is why attempts to reset those marks give only temporary results.

He links this to a 2026 Shanghai study that found a 71-terahertz vibration in mitochondria which disappears when they are dried or disrupted. Kruse reads it as a timing signal from mitochondria to the nucleus that paces telomeres and gene reading while the membrane holds its charge. When the cell's structured water collapses from his healthy "160" state to ordinary "78" water, electrons slow, the signal goes quiet and the nucleus "goes blind." Telomeres, in his view, therefore record entropy (accumulated disorder), not age.

He ties that record to electrons. A body that gathers more of them, in his account, lives on slower time, which he links to longer life, clearer thinking and faster healing. Telomeres lengthen as electrons become plentiful, he says, notably with omega-3 fats from seafood, and shorten when nnEMF (man-made wireless and electrical fields) or disordered water drains them away.

He finds support in the South American lungfish, whose genome is about 30 times larger than ours with roughly the same number of genes.
